{{Short description|Quantitative way to compare statistical models}}

In [[statistics]], the '''deficiency''' is a measure to compare a [[statistical model]] with another statistical model. The concept was introduced in the 1960s by the French mathematician [[Lucien Le Cam]], who used it to prove an approximative version of the [[Blackwell–Sherman–Stein theorem]].<ref>{{cite journal |first=Lucien |last=Le Cam |title=Sufficiency and Approximate Sufficiency |volume=35 |journal=[[Annals of Mathematical Statistics]] |number=4 |publisher=[[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] |pages=1429 |date=1964 |doi=10.1214/aoms/1177700372 |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-mathematical-statistics/volume-35/issue-4/Sufficiency-and-Approximate-Sufficiency/10.1214/aoms/1177700372.full|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |first=Erik |last=Torgersen |title=Comparison of Statistical Experiments|publisher=Cambridge University Press, United Kingdom |date=1991 |doi=10.1017/CBO9780511666353 |pages=222–257}}</ref> Closely related is the '''Le Cam distance''', a [[Pseudometric space|pseudometric]] for the maximum deficiency between two statistical models. If the deficiency of a model <math>\mathcal{E}</math> in relation to <math>\mathcal{F}</math> is zero, then one says <math>\mathcal{E}</math> is ''better'' or ''more informative'' or ''stronger'' than <math>\mathcal{F}</math>.

== Introduction ==
Le Cam defined the statistical model more abstract than a [[probability space]] with a family of probability measures. He also didn't use the term "statistical model" and instead used the term "experiment". In his publication from 1964 he introduced the statistical experiment to a parameter set <math>\Theta</math> as a triple <math>(X,E,(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta})</math> consisting of a set <math>X</math>, a [[vector lattice]] <math>E</math> with unit <math>I</math> and a family of normalized [[positive functional]]s <math>(P_\theta)_{\theta \in \Theta}</math> on <math>E</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |first=Lucien |last=Le Cam |title=Sufficiency and Approximate Sufficiency |volume=35 |journal=[[Annals of Mathematical Statistics]] |number=4 |publisher=[[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] |pages=1421 |date=1964 |doi=10.1214/aoms/1177700372 |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-mathematical-statistics/volume-35/issue-4/Sufficiency-and-Approximate-Sufficiency/10.1214/aoms/1177700372.full|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |first=Aad |last=van der Vaart |title=The Statistical Work of Lucien Le Cam |journal=The Annals of Statistics |volume=30 |number=3 |date=2002 |pages=631–82 |jstor=2699973}}</ref> In his book from 1986 he omitted <math>E</math> and <math>X</math>.<ref name="LLC-G">{{cite book|first=Lucien |last=Le Cam |title=Asymptotic methods in statistical decision theory |series=Springer Series in Statistics |publisher=Springer, New York|date=1986 |pages=1–5 |doi=10.1007/978-1-4612-4946-7}}</ref>
This article follows his definition from 1986 and uses his terminology to emphasize the generalization.

== Formulation ==
=== Basic concepts ===
Let <math>\Theta</math> be a [[parameter space]]. Given an [[abstract L-space|abstract L<sub>1</sub>-space]] <math>(L,\|\cdot\|)</math> (i.e. a [[Banach lattice]] such that for elements <math>x,y\geq 0</math> also <math>\|x+y\|=\|x\|+\|y\|</math> holds) consisting of lineare positive functionals <math>\{P_{\theta}:\theta\in\Theta\}</math>. An ''experiment'' <math>\mathcal{E}</math> is a map <math>\mathcal{E}:\Theta \to L</math> of the form <math>\theta \mapsto P_{\theta}</math>, such that <math>\|P_{\theta}\|=1</math>. <math>L</math> is the band induced by <math>\{P_{\theta}:\theta\in\Theta\}</math> and therefore we use the notation <math>L(\mathcal{E})</math>. For a <math>\mu\in L(\mathcal{E})</math> denote the <math>\mu^{+}=\mu \vee 0=\max(\mu,0)</math>. The [[dual space|topological dual]] <math>M</math> of an L-space with the conjugated norm <math>\|u\|_M=\sup\{|\langle u,\mu\rangle|; \|\mu\|_L\leq 1\}</math> is called an ''abstract M-space''. It's also a lattice with unit defined through <math>I \mu=\|\mu^+\|_L-\|\mu^-\|_L</math> for <math>\mu\in L</math>.

Let <math>L(A)</math> and <math>L(B)</math> be two L-space of two experiments <math>A</math> and <math>B</math>, then one calls a positive, norm-preserving [[linear map]], i.e. <math>\|T\mu^{+}\|=\|\mu^{+}\|</math> for all <math>\mu\in L(A)</math>, a transition. The adjoint of a transitions is a positive linear map from the dual space <math>M_B</math> of <math>L(B)</math> into the dual space <math>M_A</math> of <math>L(A)</math>, such that the unit of <math>M_A</math> is the image of the unit of <math>M_B</math> ist.<ref name="LLC-G" />

=== Deficiency ===
Let <math>\Theta</math> be a parameter space and <math>\mathcal{E}:\theta \to P_\theta</math> and <math>\mathcal{F}:\theta \to Q_\theta</math> be two experiments indexed by <math>\Theta</math>. Le <math>L(\mathcal{E})</math> and <math>L(\mathcal{F})</math> denote the corresponding L-spaces and let <math>\mathcal{T}</math> be the set of all transitions from <math>L(\mathcal{E})</math> to <math>L(\mathcal{F})</math>.

The '''deficiency''' <math>\delta(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F})</math> of <math>\mathcal{E}</math> in relation to <math>\mathcal{F}</math> is the number defined in terms of [[inf sup]]:
:<math>\delta(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F}):=\inf\limits_{T\in \mathcal{T}}\sup\limits_{\theta \in \Theta} \tfrac{1}{2}\|Q_{\theta}-TP_{\theta}\|_{\text{TV}},</math><ref name="LLC-D">{{cite book|first=Lucien |last=Le Cam |date=1986 |doi=10.1007/978-1-4612-4946-7 |publisher=Springer, New York |pages=18–19 |series=Springer Series in Statistics |title=Asymptotic methods in statistical decision theory}}</ref>
where <math>\|\cdot\|_{\text{TV}}</math> denoted the [[Total variation#Modern definition of total variation norm|total variation norm]] <math>\|\mu\|_{\text{TV}}=\mu^{+}+\mu^{-}</math>. The factor <math>\tfrac{1}{2}</math> is just for computational purposes and is sometimes omitted.
==== Explanations ====
* <math>\delta(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F})=0</math> means that there exists a transition <math>T</math> such that <math>TP_{\theta}=Q_{\theta}</math> for all <math>\theta \in \Theta</math>.
* The deficiency measures how well <math>Q_{\theta}</math> of <math>P_{\theta}</math> can be approximated by <math>T</math> in the sense of total variation.
* The deficiency is a norm for <math>Q_{\theta}-TP_{\theta}</math>.

=== Le Cam distance ===
The '''Le Cam distance''' is the following pseudometric
:<math>\Delta(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F}):= \operatorname{max}\left(\delta(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F}),\delta(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{E})\right). </math>
This induces an [[equivalence relation]] and when <math>\Delta(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F})=0</math>, then one says <math>\mathcal{E}</math> and <math>\mathcal{F}</math> are ''equivalent''. The equivalent class <math>C_{\mathcal{E}}</math> of <math>\mathcal{E}</math> is also called the ''type of <math>\mathcal{E}</math>''.

Often one is interested in families of experiments <math>(\mathcal{E}_n)_{n}</math> with <math>\{P_{n,\theta}\colon \theta \in \Theta_{n}\}</math> and <math>(\mathcal{F}_n)_{n}</math> with <math>\{Q_{n,\theta}\colon \theta \in \Theta_{n}\}</math>. If <math>\Delta(\mathcal{E}_n,\mathcal{F}_n)=0</math> as <math>n\to \infty</math>, then one says <math>(\mathcal{E}_n)</math> and <math>(\mathcal{F}_n)</math> are ''asymptotically equivalent''.

Let <math>\Theta</math> be a parameter space and <math>E(\Theta)</math> be the set of all types that are induced by <math>\Theta</math>, then the Le Cam distance <math>\Delta</math> is complete with respect to <math>E(\Theta)</math>. The condition <math>\delta(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F})=0</math> induces a [[partial order]] on <math>E(\Theta)</math>, one says <math>\mathcal{E}</math> is ''better'' or ''more informative'' or ''stronger'' than <math>\mathcal{F}</math>.<ref name="LLC-D" />
